newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes up but profit taking hits gains.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes up but profit taking hits gains.

text.p: Precious metal markets firmed on Tuesday afternoon although profit-taking soon swept them from intraday highs.
Even gold came off its recent low struck earlier on Tuesday and was fixed in the afternoon at $339.40 per ounce . This was against an earlier $338.85 which was a fresh low from April 22, 1993.
But the sector generally showed its vulnerability when the funds took their profits from recent gains by palladium and to a lesser degree silver.
These metals had had the role of providing a relatively cheap entry to the sector for speculators over the past few days, dealers said.
"Silver had proved it could resist weakness in gold which made its upside look attractive and palladium was rising on the Russian issue. The funds like these kind of markets," one said.

Russia, the major exporter, and Japan which is its principal customer, have yet to begin discussing their 1997 supply contract which has led consumers and, latterly, speculators to enter the free market.
But palladium's rise of around nine dollars in the past four trading days tempted the speculators to cash in their gains on Tuesday.
Palladium was indicated at $131.50/$132.50 shortly after the 1500 GMT gold fixes which was down from a day's high of $135.75/$136.75 and a close on Monday of $135.25/$136.25.
Gold was pressured under good volume selling earlier, which some dealers said was either from a central bank or a major producer.
At the same time borrowing rates climbed.
"With the amount of shorts in the market you would expect them to be higher than they are unless the shorts, for example are covered in the OTC (over the counter) market," an analyst said.
Others opined the one-month rate reflected gold being borrowed to be sold on behalf of a producer or a central bank.
Platinum was also off its day's high at $353.20/$354.20 and down 30 cents from the close.
"Gold's floor seems to have held for the moment against some good selling earlier which may be encouraging a bit of short covering," a dealer said.
